subject: health
title: Explicit model: body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests
focus: body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests
essentialQuestion: How do I speak up for myself, respect others, and repair a relationship after conflict?
materials: paper and pencil or an accessible response tool
the fictional lesson cards included in this task
keyPoints: Your body belongs to you; you decide about hugs, tickling, and touch, including with family.
The parts covered by a swimsuit are private.
Use correct anatomical names — they make you easier to understand and to believe.
No one should touch, look at, photograph, or ask to see your private parts, except a doctor or nurse checking your health with your guardian present, or a carer helping you when you need help.
Unsafe requests most often come from someone already known and trusted, not from a stranger — so the rule applies to everyone.
Bribes, threats, and "this is our secret" are warning signs.
If it happens it is never your fault, whatever you did, accepted, or agreed to earlier.
Tell a trusted adult and keep telling until someone helps.
privacySafeScenario: All required evidence uses fictional or public situations. The learner never has to disclose personal health, body, treatment, feelings, family, sexual, or substance-use information.
studentTask: Write two facts. Use the lesson idea about body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests. Choose one safe next step. Name an adult or help source.
knowledgeCheck: Name the fact. Fix the wrong claim. Choose a safe action. Name who can help.
completionCriteria: I explain body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests.
I choose a safe action and give a reason.
I name the right kind of help.
adaptationChoices: Show one short direction at a time. Allow reading aloud, word cards, typing, writing, drawing with labels, signing, selecting, or speaking. Help may repeat a direction but may not choose the fact, action, reason, or help source.
extensionChallenge: Create a new fictional or public case about body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests. Include enough facts, choices or constraints, and support authority for another learner to reason safely. Add an accurate explanation of acceptable variation; use no real person's private information.
accessibilitySupports: Show one action at a time.
Offer a vocabulary card and extra time.
Accept typing, writing, drawing with labels, signing, selecting, or speaking for equal credit.
trustedAdultNote: If a real situation feels unsafe or raises a health concern, pause the lesson and tell a parent, guardian, teacher, school staff member, or another trusted adult. A qualified health professional gives medical advice. In an emergency, get an adult and use the local emergency service.

optionalReflection.prompt: Optional and private: Make up one example that helps you remember body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests. Keep it for yourself. You do not need to show it or prove that you completed it.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, body-fat percentage, body comparison, or appearance scoring.
This task never requires calorie counting, dieting, or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires sharing medical history, a diagnosis, treatment, medication, feelings, family conflict, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
This task never requires advice about an individual learner's treatment, medication, food, supplement, or exercise plan.

paragraphs: Your body belongs to you; you decide about hugs, tickling, and touch, including with family.

explanation.importantDistinction: Learning about body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests supports accurate reasoning and safe next steps; it does not authorize a diagnosis, individualized treatment advice, a person label, or a value judgment.
explanation.decisionRule: NOTICE the situation. STATE the message briefly. LEAVE or pause if safety changes. TELL the responsible adult or help source.

vocabularyCheck.heading: Check the words
vocabularyCheck.selfCheck: A complete check uses the meaning of body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests, one accurate fact, and the responsible support route without labeling a person.

canonicalPracticeContext.heading: Use the authored practice situation
canonicalPracticeContext.situation: An adult a family knows well asks Sam to sit on their lap and keep it "just between us." Name every warning sign, and say exactly what Sam should do.
canonicalPracticeContext.treatment: This canonical context may support teaching or discussion. It does not replace the separate fresh independent, mastery, or remediation-retry cases.

modelExample.heading: Watch the reasoning: body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests
modelExample.situation: In a fictional Northside activity about body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests, Sam says, “I need this to stop, and I want help from the adult leading this activity.” Another participant keeps asking for private reasons. The lesson fact is: Your body belongs to you; you decide about hugs, tickling, and touch, including with family.
relevantFacts: Your body belongs to you; you decide about hugs, tickling, and touch, including with family.
The parts covered by a swimsuit are private.
modelExample.assumptionOrDistraction: A popular or confident statement about body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests is not automatically accurate and cannot establish a person's health, motives, or character.
possibleActions: Respect the brief message, stop pressing for details, and involve the responsible adult.
Require a private explanation before respecting the request.
Make the peer responsible for solving the entire situation.
modelExample.successCheck: The model uses the lesson fact, explains the connection, stays within the learner role, and names responsible help when it is needed.
workedReasoning: Use a short message such as: “I need help with this situation about body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests. Here is the fact I know and the safe next step I am asking for.”
Do not require the fictional person to justify a boundary or reveal private details.
If pressure, danger, or urgency increases, end the exchange and contact the responsible adult or service.

guidedReasoning.heading: Try a different case with support
guidedReasoning.situation: A fictional Riverside youth group must explain or act on body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests. The group has this reliable lesson information: The parts covered by a swimsuit are private. It has not been given any person's private health information.
availableChoices: State or respect a brief message and contact responsible help.
turnOne: Name an adult who can help.
guidedReasoning.cue: Look for the fact, the brief message, the boundary of the learner role, and the help route.
feedbackMoves: If a response adds a guess, replace it with a fact from the case or lesson.
If body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests is named without explanation, link one fact to the concept or process.
If a choice is reasonable but the reason is missing, add the fact that supports it.
If a response seeks disclosure, diagnoses, shames, or exceeds the learner role, switch to the fictional facts and the approved help route.
Accept an equivalent typed, handwritten, drawn-and-labeled, signed, selected, or spoken response when it shows the same reasoning.
guidedReasoning.turnTwo: Fix one sentence. Use a fact and a safe next step.
guidedReasoning.releaseCondition: Continue when the response uses a stated fact, applies body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests, and gives a safe next step without private disclosure or a person label.

typing, writing, drawing with labels, signing, selecting, or speaking

freshMasteryCheck.heading: Check the idea in a new place
freshMasteryCheck.situation: A fictional Lakeside school committee reviews body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests. The committee knows: Use correct anatomical names — they make you easier to understand and to believe. It must correct one unsupported claim and choose a safe next step.
freshMasteryCheck.freshnessNote: This case is different from the model, guided case, and independent case. Do not copy their conclusions.

remediation.heading: Try a different model
remediation.trigger: Use this route after an observable gap in a fact, vocabulary meaning, reasoning step, process order, or help route for body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests.
remediation.prerequisite: First restate this approved fact in your own words: Your body belongs to you; you decide about hugs, tickling, and touch, including with family.
remediation.alternateExplanation: Use a three-box message map: FACT I can state, MESSAGE or LIMIT I can say, and HELP I can contact. Private details stay outside the boxes because they are not needed to practice the skill.
contrast: Sufficient: uses a stated fact about body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests, explains the connection, and stays within the learner role.
Needs revision: repeats a topic word, adds a guess, or gives an action with no factual reason or responsible help source.
remediation.guidedCorrection: Cross out the guess. Circle the fact. Add one safe action.

freshRetry.situation: A fictional Oak Street library receives a new question about body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests. Staff provide this approved fact: The parts covered by a swimsuit are private. The learner must respond without using the Northside, Riverside, Maple, or Lakeside conclusions.

remediation.exitCriterion: Return to the independent route when the learner accurately uses a fact, applies body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests, explains a safe response, and identifies support without answer-bearing help.
remediation.nextRoute: If the same gap remains, return to the named prerequisite with an adult instructor; do not replace the task with private reflection.

laterTransfer.timing: Use in a later lesson or a separate session.
laterTransfer.prompt: Apply body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests to a meaningfully different fictional or public case. Retrieve the concept, use relevant facts, justify a safe response, and identify the responsible support or authority route.
laterTransfer.masteryBoundary: The current independent response is one evidence occasion. Mastery requires accurate independent evidence now and accurate later retrieval or transfer.
